function.arguments: {"headline":"Plan type and churn: Enterprise vs Starter","findings":[{"statement":"In the development sample, Enterprise accounts have a slightly lower churn rate (44.23%) than Starter accounts (44.58%), but the 95% confidence interval for the rate difference spans -9.07 to +8.58 percentage points, making the difference statistically insignificant (p = 0.94).","kind":"association","evidence":["E4","E5"]},{"statement":"When controlling for billing_cycle, annual subscribers churn at 30.56% versus 56.46% for monthly subscribers, indicating billing cycle has a stronger association with churn than plan type.","kind":"association","evidence":["E6"]},{"statement":"Cramér's V for plan is 0.0434, ranking it among the weakest single‑feature associations with churn, behind login_change_pct (0.277), billing_cycle (0.253), and failed_payments_90d (0.213).","kind":"association","evidence":["E2"]},{"statement":"The logistic regression model trained on the development set achieves an average precision of 0.785, indicating moderate predictive power but no feature, including plan, can be said to cause churn.","kind":"model_performance","evidence":["E3"]},{"statement":"NPS and support tickets show moderate associations with churn (Cramér's V 0.176 and 0.111 respectively), while seats and active_users_30d show weak associations (V < 0.06).","kind":"association","evidence":["E2"]}],"caveats":["Confidence intervals are wide for some segments, reflecting small subgroup sizes.","All findings describe historical associations; no causation is implied.","Missing data for NPS (19.6% share) may affect related analyses."],"next_steps":["Re‑run the churn comparison after imputing or removing the high‑missing NPS field.","Test whether adding billing_cycle and failed_payments_90d to a model reduces the plan coefficient, suggesting confounding.","Collect additional historical data or run a randomized experiment to isolate the plan‑churn relationship."]}
